source_document.body:
Apple announced new agreements with U.S. suppliers, including a commitment of up to $100 million over three years with Pennsylvania titanium producer Perryman Company. The metal will go into Apple products, including the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone.
What’s Related
Apple is also expanding its work with Delaware-based Qnity Electronics, which will manufacture films used in the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera system. Both partnerships are part of Apple’s American Manufacturing Program, launched last year.
The announcement covers materials and components for Apple’s latest phones. Apple says American companies produce nearly 100 components used in the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, drawing from suppliers in more than a dozen states.
“We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer.
RELATED STORIES: Apple Expands U.S. Supply Chain with $400 Million Investment | Where iPhones Really Come From: A Look at Apple’s Global Supply Chain
Titanium production in Pennsylvania
Perryman, a family-owned manufacturer, melts, forges, and rolls titanium at its facility in Houston, Pennsylvania. The titanium it supplies for the iPhone Duo contains at least 80% recycled material and is used in the phone’s grade 5 titanium enclosure.
Qnity’s films will be used in the iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture camera system, which adjusts how much light enters the camera. The company joined Apple’s American Manufacturing Program in March.
Apple did not disclose the value of the expanded Qnity agreement or production volumes for either supplier. The manufacturing program is part of its previously announced $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation .
More glass and chips from U.S. factories
Apple also provided updates on several existing suppliers, including projects involving glass, wireless components, and semiconductor production:
Corning: By the end of 2026, its Harrodsburg, Kentucky, facility will produce all cover glass for iPhones and Apple Watches sold worldwide.
Broadcom: A $1.5 billion expansion and modernization project in Fort Collins, Colorado, will make radio frequency components. Apple’s multiyear agreement with Broadcom is expected to produce more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips.
TSMC : Its Arizona factory is producing more than 100 million chips for Apple in 2026.
Coherent : Its Sherman, Texas , facility supplies laser technology used for Face ID and other device features.
Chip packaging and training
Apple will also be among the first customers of Amkor Technology’s semiconductor packaging and testing facility in Peoria, Arizona. Amkor broke ground in September 2025 and began building the facility’s shell this year; the first two phases are expected to create more than 3,500 local jobs .
Separately, Apple opened a 20,000-square-foot manufacturing training center in Houston, Texas, in August. Apple engineers teach smaller businesses about final assembly and circuit board manufacturing at the site, which shares a building with Apple’s AI server production and planned Mac mini manufacturing.
